property_summary: When the owner calls AdjustBetAmounts(amount), the contract's currentBetLimit() equals the provided amount (i.e., AdjustBetAmounts sets betLimit to amount rather than incrementing it).

For any nonzero amount, calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) on the correct contract sets betLimit equal to exactly amount (overwriting previous), whereas the mutant increments betLimit so betLimit != amount for some inputs; the property asserts that after calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) the contract's currentBetLimit() equals amount.

For any fuzzed uint256 amount, calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) on the reference contract sets betLimit exactly to amount (overwriting previous); the mutant that increments instead will make currentBetLimit() != amount for some inputs, so asserting currentBetLimit() == amount distinguishes them.

For any uint256 amount, after calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) on a freshly-deployed contract, the contract's currentBetLimit() equals amount (reference overwrites betLimit; the mutant that increments breaks this for inputs where initial betLimit != 0).

For any initial nonzero betLimit (set at deployment) and any fuzzed uint256 delta, calling AdjustBetAmounts(delta) by the owner increases the bet limit by exactly delta (i.e., new betLimit == oldBetLimit + delta) — the reference sets betLimit to the provided amount when initial was zero but with a nonzero initial betLimit this additive property holds for the reference while the mutant that adds again will break equality for some inputs (we instead assert the general rule that when starting from a nonzero initial betLimit, calling AdjustBetAmounts with any amount results in currentBetLimit() != 0 and equals old + amount), and the mutant will violate this for some fuzzed amounts.

For any nonzero initial betLimit (set by deploying C with a nonzero wagerLimit), calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) by the owner sets currentBetLimit() equal to the provided amount (i.e., it overwrites prior value); the mutant that increments instead will make currentBetLimit() != amount for some fuzzed amounts, so asserting equality to amount distinguishes them.

After owner calls AdjustBetAmounts(x) and then anyone opens and wagers the betLimit, the contract's currentBetLimit() equals the value required to successfully place a wager (so hasPlayerWagered can become true after wager and play sequence), i.e., AdjustBetAmounts must set a nonzero bet limit allowing wager() to accept the provided amount.
After play() is called by a player who previously wagered, calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) must not set currentBetLimit() to zero when the contract previously accepted a nonzero wager.
Calling AdjustBetAmounts after play must not reduce the contract's winnersPot() (half the balance) to zero when play previously allowed a valid wager that could lead to a nonzero pot.

After a successful play() call by a player, calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) must not make currentBetLimit() different from the previous betLimit if the play consumed the prior wager (i.e., currentBetLimit remains equal to the value that allowed the wager).
Calling AdjustBetAmounts after play preserves that the contract's winnersPot() remains strictly positive whenever play could have been called successfully (i.e., play did not revert).

For any owner-supplied amount, calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) sets c.currentBetLimit() equal to that amount; the mutant always sets betLimit to 0 so for some non-zero amount the post-call bet limit differs.

For any nonzero wagerLimit input passed to AdjustBetAmounts by the owner, the reference contract sets betLimit to that input while the mutant sets it to 0 (so after the call, c.currentBetLimit() == amount for all amounts, but mutant yields 0 for some nonzero amounts).

For any owner-caller and any uint256 amount, after calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) the reference contract's currentBetLimit() equals the provided amount; the mutant sets betLimit to 0 regardless, so for some nonzero amounts the mutant's currentBetLimit() != amount (test uses fuzzed amount and owner call to detect this).

For any caller that is the contract owner, calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) sets the contract's public currentBetLimit() to the provided amount; the mutant always sets betLimit to 0 so for some nonzero amounts currentBetLimit() != amount and the property is violated.

For any owner caller and any uint256 newLimit, after calling AdjustBetAmounts(newLimit) the reference contract's currentBetLimit() equals newLimit, whereas the mutant sets betLimit to 0 and thus will differ for some nonzero newLimit.
Only the owner can call AdjustBetAmounts (so calling it from a non-owner will revert), i.e., AdjustBetAmounts succeeds when invoked by the contract owner and fails when invoked by any other address.
